assignment: Design a short calibration exercise for reviewers selecting student projects.
source: Four reviewers each rated ten different projects on a five-point scale. Reviewers' mean ratings range from 2.8 to 4.1. Each reviewer saw one subject area only. A second round can afford 24 ratings on eight anonymized projects. The committee wants to distinguish severity differences from project quality and keep a usable appeals record.

criteria.full: Explains why the first-round reviewer means confound subject matter, project mix and reviewer severity.
criteria.partial: Treats the difference in means as a direct severity estimate.

criteria.full: Uses the 24 ratings as three per project or an equally defensible connected overlapping design with explicit counts.
criteria.partial: Proposes double rating without reconciling ratings and connectivity.

criteria.full: Defines anchors, blinded independent scoring and a way to examine within-project disagreement or reviewer effects.
criteria.partial: Suggests a group discussion without independent comparisons.

criteria.full: Defines how discrepancies are adjudicated, records rationale and limits the generalization from eight projects.
criteria.partial: Overstates precision or omits an auditable appeal path.
